title: Stop partner uploads from reading files on the import host

blocks.text: Partners upload their orders as XML files into the import directory, and the import parses each one with the JDK's DOM parser. The same disk holds the import host's own configuration, and partners' systems keep files of declarations next to their orders. A partner's upload account is a password that more than one person knows.

Partner orders are plain XML: elements, attributes and text. Write `newFactory()` in `src/main/java/practice/OrderImport.java` so that a plain order is read as before, and no upload can make the import read another file into the order or load declarations from one. When the parser refuses a document, the `SAXException` it throws may reach the caller.

cases.says: a plain order document is read: its attribute, items and note, with a character reference
an entity declared in the document with a SYSTEM file does not put that file's text into the order
a parameter entity naming a file does not load the declarations in it
a DOCTYPE naming an external DTD file does not load it, even when the parser keeps entity references unexpanded

origin.section: The JDK's XML Parsers Read External Entities Until You Turn Them Off

concepts: The JDK's default DocumentBuilderFactory reads a file named by an external entity into the result; disallow-doctype-decl, or ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD set to "", refuses it.
